plain.text: Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the Lord's disciples. He got letters from the high priest to arrest any followers of "the Way" in Damascus. As he neared Damascus, a light from heaven suddenly flashed around him. He fell to the ground and heard a voice: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?" "Who are you, Lord?" "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting. Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do." Saul got up, but when he opened his eyes he could see nothing. For three days he was blind and did not eat or drink.

In Damascus a disciple named Ananias had a vision. The Lord told him to go to Saul, who was praying. Ananias was afraid: he had heard how much harm Saul had done. But the Lord said, "Go! This man is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the Gentiles and their kings and to the people of Israel." Ananias went, placed his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit." Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see. He got up and was baptised, and after eating, he regained his strength.

At once Saul began to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God. Everyone was astonished: "Isn't he the man who caused havoc in Jerusalem?" Saul grew more and more powerful and baffled his opponents by proving that Jesus is the Messiah.
After many days, some plotted to kill him and watched the city gates day and night. But his followers took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the wall.

In Jerusalem, Saul tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him. Barnabas took him to the apostles and told them how Saul had seen the Lord and preached fearlessly in Damascus. So Saul stayed with them and spoke boldly in the name of the Lord. When some tried to kill him, the believers sent him off to Tarsus.

Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee and Samaria enjoyed a time of peace and was strengthened. Living in the fear of the Lord and encouraged by the Holy Spirit, it increased in numbers. In Lydda, Peter found a man named Aeneas who had been paralysed and bedridden for eight years. "Jesus Christ heals you. Get up!" Immediately he got up, and many turned to the Lord.

In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (Dorcas), always doing good and helping the poor. She became sick and died. The disciples sent for Peter. Widows showed him the clothes she had made. Peter sent them out, knelt and prayed, and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes and sat up. This became known all over Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus himself stops Saul, the persecutor, and turns him into a messenger of the good news.
points: On the road to Damascus, the risen Jesus confronts Saul.
Ananias overcomes his fear and calls Saul "Brother".
Barnabas vouches for Saul; Peter heals Aeneas and raises Tabitha.
summary.reflection: Ananias and Barnabas welcomed someone others feared. Who might need you to give them a second chance?
